en.def: HTML5 standard for defining new HTML tags with their own behavior, registered via customElements.define(). Browsers parse them as ordinary DOM nodes.
Encapsulated DOM subtree attached to a host element. Styles and IDs inside don't leak out; styles outside don't leak in.
Flash of Unstyled Content. Brief moment when a page renders before its CSS or component styling applies. Mitigated by inlining critical CSS or pre-paint scripts.
The user-visible region of a web page. Distinct from the layout viewport (which is the document size) and the visual viewport (which moves under pinch-zoom).
Browser API exposing the user-visible viewport during pinch-zoom. window.visualViewport.offsetLeft/offsetTop give the visual viewport's offset relative to the layout viewport.
CSS media query that reflects the user's OS theme preference (light or dark). Updates live when the OS theme changes.
Browser-side key/value persistence scoped to origin. ~5 MB per origin. Synchronous API; persists across sessions.
pushState / replaceState / popstate for client-side URL changes without page reload. Enables clean-URL routing in SPAs.
API for observing when elements enter or leave the viewport. Replaces hand-rolled scroll-listener gymnastics for visibility detection.
Custom property declared with --name: value and read with var(--name). Cascades like any property; can be updated at runtime via style.setProperty.
